learning_outcomes.statement: The learner can create, index, slice, and mutate lists; distinguish aliasing from copying (including the shallow-copy nuance); and use tuples for immutable, unpackable records.

The learner can use sets (including full Venn-diagram algebra and hashability), dicts (including nested structures and nine core methods), comprehensions, and a complete decision map to choose the right collection for a scenario.

criteria.rationale: Three defects were found and fixed during this batch: F-008a/F-008b (MINOR, two stale hashability error-message quotes) and F-009 (MINOR, a mutate-during-iteration example that failed to visibly demonstrate its own point); every other claim, including all set-algebra, shallow/deep-copy, and comprehension results, was independently re-executed under Python 3.14.6 and confirmed correct.
All list/tuple/set/dict method behavior (sort()-returns-None, append-vs-extend, shallow-copy sharing, dict insertion-order guarantee since 3.7) verified against the actual Python 3.14.6 interpreter.

Precise terminology throughout (изменяемость/неизменяемость extended from string to list/tuple, aliasing, поверхностная копия, хешируемость); register entries added for all of these, extending rather than contradicting the Batch B string-immutability entry.

The opener promises list/tuple/set/dict fundamentals, mutability/aliasing/copying, comprehensions, structure-selection, debugging, and multiple mini-projects; all delivered with no gap once the three content defects were fixed.

All grader-relied-upon claims (set operations, dict method results, comprehension outputs) independently re-executed and match exactly; the two hashability-error corrections were independently verified against live Python 3.14.6 error text.
Concrete, checkable scope (build a contact book, count word frequency, choose the right structure for a scenario) rather than vague aspirations.

Assumes only Chapters 1-10; every new term (aliasing, shallow copy, hashability) is introduced before use, and the chapter's own decision map is explicitly labeled provisional (11-11) until completed (11-23).
Opens with a concrete pain point (500 separate score_N variables) before introducing collections as the solution.
27 sections chunked into clear sub-arcs (lists -> mutability/aliasing/copying -> tuples -> sets -> dicts -> nested structures/comprehensions -> structure selection -> debugging -> mini-projects).

11-24's 14-named-bug catalog and the closing 11-10 toolkit recap, plus an evidence-based bridge to Chapter 12 functions (citing specific duplicated code across the chapter's own projects), provide genuine consolidation.
Terminology used identically across all 27 sections; correctly extends the Batch A/B mutability register rather than restating it inconsistently.
All internal cross-references verified to point to sections that exist and contain the referenced content.
The [[0]*3]*3 trap and the aliasing converge-diagram idiom are explicitly and correctly reused between 11-04 and 11-16 rather than being independently reinvented.
Chapter number, title, and all 27 section identifiers match the PAGES navigation model and sidebar exactly.
